Issued at 237 AM EST Fri Nov 27 2026

A broad negative mid/upper level negative height anomaly will 
slowly track northeast today into northeast CONUS. Stronger 
upper dynamics are favored well southeast of the local area, but
residence time of this negative height anomaly is being 
prolonged locally by tendency of large scale diabatic PV anomaly
to displace the mid level height minimum to the northwest 
across northeast Kentucky/southern Ohio. While best upper jet 
dynamics will continue to shift across Mid Atlantic this 
morning, the separated interior PV anomaly across the Ohio 
Valley will exhibit only slow northeast progression today. This 
should prolong some weak isentropic forcing today, particularly 
across far northeast Indiana/northwest Ohio/south central Lower 
Michigan. Some weak deformation forcing associated with this 
lagging PV anomaly could also enhance precip later this morning 
into this afternoon particularly along and east of the I-69 
corridor. Additional precip chances will exist from western 
Lower Michigan into northwest Indiana tied more to sheared 
vorticity filament on western fringe of this system, where also 
some weak low level frontogenesis will likely play some 
continued role where remnants of a weak TROWAL signature should 
persist into this afternoon.

Increased low level lift since early last evening has likely 
contributed to some weak low level cooling that could raise some 
ptype concerns with indications in higher res near term models of 
925 mb wet bulb temps just below freezing through daybreak. The
complicating factor for realizing any mixing in of wet snow 
this morning will be likely maintenance of sfc wet bulbs just 
above freezing for most areas. Current indications would suggest
that best chance of mixing in some wet snow may be across 
northeast portions of the of forecast area where sfc wet bulbs 
will likely be a bit lower from NE IN into SE Lower MI, and 
where some brief stronger lift with any deformation-forced 
precip, could steer precip types briefly to some wet snow mixing
in during period of strongest lift. Sfc wet bulbs may remain a 
bit higher across the west, although cannot completely rule out 
some brief wet snow mixing in this morning if any axes of 
stronger low level fgen can come into play especially across SW 
Lower Michigan. Forecast thinking from previous cycles remains 
intact in that any snow accumulation would likely only be a 
tenth or two across grassy areas this morning, with roads 
remaining wet. Most areas should not receive any snow
accumulation.

For tonight, lingering light rain may persist for eastern locations 
early evening as last mid level trough axis pushes across the area. 
This will be followed by approach of some induced short wave mid 
level ridging in advance of next upper trough tracking across 
the Upper Midwest. Stronger forcing with this feature looks to 
remain across the central/northern Great Lakes on Saturday, and 
while some mid level moisture is likely to increase with this 
feature Saturday AM, subcloud layer appears to be too dry to 
support mentionable PoPs at this time. Otherwise, some increase 
in sun is expected by PM as mid level clouds push east and 
modest low level warm advection should support some moderation 
in temps back into mid/upper 40s for Saturday afternoon.

Attention will then turn to a digging wave from Pacific NW for 
Saturday night into Sunday. It does appear as though both advective 
and deformation forcing components will accompany this short wave. 
Typically by this time of year, the expected suppressed track 
of low level reflection of this system would support some wintry
precip, but this pattern looks to be characterized by continued
lack of any immediate northern latitude phasing, with push of 
cold air appearing a bit too delayed for anything more than rain
with this system. It is possible at very tail end of precip, 
some wet snow could briefly mix in Sunday evening, but this 
potential appears too low for a mention at this time. Colder and
blustery conditions follow behind the associated cold front for
Sunday night into Monday with Monday likely to feature coldest 
conditions of this period.

Not much change was warranted for the later periods with higher 
confidence in a warmup through the work week and mainly dry 
conditions through Thursday. Medium range models are in general 
agreement of larger scale southern stream wave evolving in split-
flow across western CONUS, eventually leading to better rain chances 
heading into late Thursday/Friday.
